## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One Important defect needs fixing: when `--json` comes right before another flag, `--json` takes that flag as its path. This breaks the combination the description promises, using `--json` "alongside the required --junit destination", whenever `--json` comes first. This review read both changed files in full and traced `parse_args` and `write_reports` through the flag orderings the PR description implies. No tests were run. The `--junit` change keeps the earlier missing-path check, and the added tests cover both of its error paths: a bare `--junit` and `--junit --json`.

## Changes
This PR adds a `--json` option to `parse_args`, which writes to `results.json` when no path is given or to an explicit path when one is. It also adds `write_reports`, which writes each parsed report to its destination, and a new `tests/test_cli.py`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/cli.py:15 — correctness — Don't treat a following flag as the JSON path — `parse_args(["--json", "--junit", "out.xml"])` sets `json` to `"--junit"` and then fails with `ValueError("unknown option: out.xml")`. The cause is that lines 15–19 accept any next argument as the destination. They don't check for a leading `--` the way the `--junit` branch does on line 7. — Users who put `--json` before `--junit` get a confusing error about their JUnit path, and neither report is written. The same happens with any later flag, which the parser takes as a filename. This also makes the comment on line 12 ("JSON can use its default destination when no path is supplied") false for that input. The added tests only check `--json` alone or with an explicit path, so they don't catch this. — Fix: Use the default destination when `args[i + 1].startswith("--")`, as line 7 does, and add a test for `["--json", "--junit", "x.xml"]` that expects `{"json": "results.json", "junit": "x.xml"}`.
